This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 to 3 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 08.01.2022 at about 5.45 p.m. petitioner had been going as a pillion rider on Honda Activa Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-07-ED-6852 being ridden by his son Raghavendra Setty in betweetn N.Vaddahalli- M.Venkatapura Gate, NH-75 road,
Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar, at that time, a car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5983 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Honda Activa from behind, thereafter dashed against one XL vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-W-4257.
Due to the said impact, petitioner fell down along with rider and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, thereafter shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as SCCH-5 inpatient, for which he has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 63 years, hale and healthy, running grocery shop,
thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is unable to continue his business,
thereby he has lost his earnings.

Out of this accident crime No.6/2022 is registered against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ML-5983 before the Nangli Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are insurers and R3 being the owner of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
SCCH-5 4.
On service of notice, Respondent No.1 and 2/insurers have appeared and filed written statement.

It is submitted that, respondent No.1/Bharati AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd., has transferred its general insurance business to respondent No.2/ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company by way of a demerger pursuant to a scheme of Arrangement under provisions of Companies Act, 2013.

Respondent No.2 further submitted that, as per the police records, it is a hit and run case and there is delay in lodging the complaint and the said car has been falsely SCCH-5 implicated and driver of the said car does not possessed valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.3 has appeared through Sri.SVS counsel, but not chosen to file the written statement.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, on 08.01.2022 at about 5.45 p.m. proceeding as a pillion rider on Honda Activa two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA- 07-ED-6852 in between N.Vaddahalli - M.Venkatapura Gate, NH-75 Road, Mulbagal Taluk, Kolar, at that time, a rider of XL Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- SCCH-5 07-W-4257 ridden in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's vehicle,
as a result of which petitioner fell down and he sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so from which respondent?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Vishal,
Consultant Urologist at Hosmat Hospital as PW-2, further examined Dr.Krishan Prasad,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital as PW-3, the Billing Incharge at Hosmat Hospital by name Shanthamma is examined as PW-4, further Administrative Officer by name Sambaraju Manikanta at New India Assurance Co.
SCCH-5 Ltd., is examined as PW-5 and marked 32 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.32 and closed his evidence.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not SCCH-5 reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.6, copy fo charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
9.

Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he has examined Dr.Vishal as PW-2 and Dr.Krishan Prasad as PW-3, Billing Incharge at Hosmat Hospital as PW-4 and Administrative Officer of the New India Assurance Co. Ltd., as PW-5 and the records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint,
sketch, spot mahazar, IMV Report, seizure mahazar and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 0801.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 10.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 08.01.2022 at about 5.45 p.m. while he was proceeding as pillion rider on Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA-07-ED-6852 in between N.Vaddahalli- M.Venktarapura Gate, NH-75 Road,
Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident SCCH-5 is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained closed displaced left superior and inferior pubic rami fracture with pubic diastasis and anterior colomn fracture acetabulum with right SI joint disruption, right parietal sub arachnoid haemorrhage with left frontal bone fractrue,
facio- maxillary injury, urethral injury.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8 issued by R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as inpatient Betaiah Shetty vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175016068/
4 since 08.01.2022 to 10.01.2022, SCCH-5 thereafter he took treatment as inpatient at Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru for 5 times i.e., from 10.01.2022 to 14.01.2022, 03.03.2022 to 04.03.2022,
20.04.2022 to 23.04.2022, 01.09.2022 to 03.09.2022 and on 30.01.2023 and 01.02.2023.

13.
Dr.Vishal, Consultant Urologist at Hosmat Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited inpatient file marked as Ex.P.23 and outpatient file marked as Ex.P.24 and he has assessed whole body impairment to may by SCCH-5 involvement of the genito-urinary tract is 10%.
In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, on 01.09.2022 the right simple orchidectomy (removal of right testies) VIU and urethral dialation was done and only one testies is removed.
Further patient can survive on single testies and he can pass urine.
Further he deposed that, 10% is only impairment and not disability.
14. Dr.Krishan Prasad, Consultatn Orthopaedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital Bengaluru is examined as PW-3.
To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD File marked as Ex.P.25, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.26 and inpatient file marked as Ex.P.27.
Further he has assessed lower limb disability at the rate of 63%, which is whole body disability of 21%.
In cross- examination deposed that, there is no bone surgery.
Further deposed that, he is not a treated Doctor and he SCCH-5 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
Further deposed that, petitioner can do his day-to-day activities with difficulty.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 20% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 62% of lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. Further Billing Incharge at Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW-4 who has exhibited copy of ID Card marked as Ex.P.28 and final bills marked as Ex.P.29.
16.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 63 years, for proof of his age, he has produced SCCH-5 copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.22, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1958 and the alleged accident is occurred on 08.01.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.22 his age is considered about 64 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 7 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
17. As per his case, he was running grocery shop, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. to prove the said fact, he got exhibited tax paid receipts marked as Ex.P.9 and license marked as Ex.P.10.
Except these documents, petitioner has not furnished any income proof documents.

Under such circumstances,
with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority SCCH-5 Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss Betaiah Shetty vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175016068/
5 income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
14,750/-x12x7x20% = Rs.2,47,800/-
18.

The Administrative Officer of the New India Assurance Co. Ltd., is examined as PW-5 who exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.30, account statement details marked as Ex.P.31 and copy of policy marked as Ex.P.32.

Ofcourse during the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 Sri.G.S argued that, after the accident petitioner is running his shop and there is no loss of future income and medical bills placed for Rs.4,35,328/- has been created by the petitioner and they have taken insurance from New India Assurance Co. Ltd., in his son name, who has claimed reimbursement from his insurance company pertaining to medical bills of his father.
PW-5 is his employee, he admitted that son of the petitioner is able to claim upto Rs.2,00,000/- and on all these reasons prays to dismiss the petition.

So except oral arguments, respondents have not placed any substantial materials to disbelieve the case of the SCCH-5 petitioner including medical bill amount, running of the shop by the petitioner after occurring of the accident and also reimbursement of Rs.4,35,328/-
as argued by the respondents counsel.

As stated supra, as admitted by PW-5, Rs.29,250/- has been reimbursed by the insurance company of son of petitioner and the said amount has been deducted from medical bills of Rs.4,35,328/-, he only entitled for i.e. Rs.4,06,078/- and petitioner is also entitled for medical bills of Rs.15,797/- marked as Ex.P.19.

So that, petitioner is entitled for total medical expenses of Rs.4,21,875/-.
21.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Vema Mahesh Babu for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.
So SCCH-5 the said charge sheet Betaiah Shetty vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175016068/

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.4,21,875/-.
22.Per contra except denial in the written statement
, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Except filing of the written statement,cross-examining the PW-1 to PW-5 orally, SCCH-5 have not taken any steps to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
23. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

7 SCCH-5 ::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,22,050/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Twenty Two Thousand Fifty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-5 Draw award accordingly.
